A 5-year-old girl plunged 49 feet from a moving cruise ship into the open ocean. Her father heard his wife screaming and raced toward the railing, only to discover that their daughter was gone.

It happened aboard the Disney Dream near the Bahamas, where a family vacation took a terrifying turn when the little girl fell from the ship’s fourth deck.

When her father realized what had happened, he jumped overboard after her, plunging nearly 50 feet into the ocean. But when he surfaced, he couldn’t see his daughter anywhere.

He began desperately calling out for her, searching the water until he finally heard her calling back. He swam toward her and managed to reach her, but they were still stranded in the open ocean as the massive cruise ship began turning around.

For roughly 20 minutes, he kept his little girl afloat, holding her above the water until a rescue boat finally reached them and brought them back to safety.

Both survived, although the father suffered two fractures in his spine from the fall.

It takes an incredible amount of courage to jump nearly 50 feet into the open ocean, not knowing what awaits you below. But this father didn’t hesitate to put his own life on the line for his little girl. Thank God they both made it home.

Mortgage lenders will lose far more during the developing mortgage crisis than they did during all of the GFC. From 2007–2010, realized losses on defaulted mortgages totaled about $450 billion.

There is currently about $8.3 trillion in outstanding fixed-rate mortgages with an average rate of 4.6% and 25 years left to maturity. Given that current rates are 7.5%, the mark-to-market losses on those mortgages are already about $2 trillion. When rates rise to 8.5%, the loss will rise to $3 trillion!

That means even without a single default, on paper mortgage lenders have already lost over four times more than they lost during the GFC. That loss will grow to nearly seven times as much when mortgage rates hit 8.5%.

Worse, during the GFC, since mortgage rates plunged, lenders had mark-to-market gains on all the outstanding mortgages that did not default. Since only 10% of the mortgages defaulted, those unrealized gains totaled about $1.75 trillion. That provided a huge cushion that today's mortgage lenders no longer have. In fact, when mark-to-market gains were taken into account, mortgage lenders actually made $1.3 trillion during the GFC.

The current situation is therefore orders of magnitude worse. The impending disaster was created by the Federal Reserve holding interest rates so low for so long, and the FHA and GSEs guaranteeing 30-year fixed-rate mortgages, which allowed borrowers to lock in such low rates for such long durations. That sowed the seeds for the perfect storm of financial destruction that is about to hit.

Washington is threatening.

▸ THE CALLS

Two Ukrainian officials say their American counterparts made the position explicit: if Russian energy infrastructure is struck during the ceasefire Trump announced on October 11, Washington will hold Kyiv responsible.

The calls went to the top. Pavlo Palisa, deputy head of the Presidential Office in charge of military affairs.

Mykhailo Drapatyi, commander-in-chief of the Armed Forces.

One Ukrainian official described it directly: "They called all the top military officials with threats. They're telling everyone that they're going to turn off both the intelligence sharing and PURL."

PURL is the Priority Ukraine Requirements List, the mechanism through which American weapons are purchased for Ukraine. Intelligence sharing is the targeting data that makes precision strikes possible.

Both now serve as a means of influence.

▸ THE SEQUENCE

Kyiv was not warned in advance. Multiple senior Ukrainian officials confirmed that nobody told them Trump was about to announce an energy ceasefire on October 11.

The announcement came first. The pressure came second.

After Trump posted, Ukrainian officials were worked over the phones and told to comply. Not asked to negotiate.

Told to stop hitting Russian refineries.

Russia struck the Kharkiv thermal power plant hours after the announcement. That strike technically fits the White House framework because power plants were never covered.

Only refineries count.

▸ THE ASYMMETRY

Zelensky addressed the Warsaw Security Forum and stated the problem plainly.

Ukraine agreed to an energy ceasefire. But the American team knows what that means in practice.

Ukraine has a single oil refinery, Kremenchuk, along with limited reserves and export capacity.

It was heavily damaged by Russian strikes long ago. Importing fuel is simply Ukrainian reality.

So a refinery-for-refinery truce protects Russian war logistics while giving Ukraine nothing. Moscow keeps its refining capacity intact.

Kyiv is asked to stop hitting the one target set that actually hurts the Russian war machine.

Zelensky repeated that Ukraine will accept an energy ceasefire if it covers all energy infrastructure, including refineries. Power plants.

Grids. The things Russia actually hits.

Washington's answer so far is to threaten the country defending itself.

U.S. officials are calling Kyiv and European capitals with a warning: keep hitting Russian oil refineries and Ukraine loses intelligence sharing and the PURL program it uses to buy American weapons.

Zelensky passed on roughly six requests from the Trump administration to halt the refinery strikes.

Trump has since announced an energy ceasefire between both sides.

The U.S. Department of Labor announced it would suspend Microsoft
 and Adobe
 from its Permanent Labor Certification program on Thursday, Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling said, as the Trump administration continues to take aim at immigration and foreign hiring programs ahead of November’s midterm elections.

Sonderling said the Labor Department won’t accept or process any new applications under the program for a host of companies, including Cognizant, Infosys, Capgemini, Tata, Wipro and HCL.

The secretary said Adobe and Microsoft were also suspended “due to multiple active federal investigations.”

“Since 2009, just these companies alone have requested almost 3 million foreign workers. They’ve received over 230,000 H-1B visas approvals and over 100,000 permanent labor certifications. That’s hundreds of thousands of jobs that were taken from American workers,” Sonderling said.
